card.statement:
We call a rational family of bounded minimal complexes over $\bA$ a bounded complex $(P_\bp,d_\bp)$ of finitely generated projective $\bA\*\sR$-modules, where $\sR$ is a rational algebra, i.e. $\sR=\Mk[t,f(t)^{-1}]$ for a nonzero polynomial $f(t)$, and $\im d_n\subseteq\sJ P_{n-1}$, where $\sJ=\rad\bA$. For a rational family $(P_\bp,d_\bp)$ we define the complex $P_\bp(m,\la)=(P_\bp\*_\sR\sR/(t-\la)^m,d_\bp\*1)$ of projective $\bA$-modules, where $m\in\mN,\,\la\in\Mk,\,f(\la)\ne0$. Set $\fR_\bp(P_\bp)=
 \fR_\bp(P_\bp(1,\la))$ ($\fR_\bp$ does not depend on $\la$).

- We call an algebra $\bA$ derived tame if there is a set $\dP$ of rational families of bounded complexes over $\bA$ such that:

- For each vector rank $\fR_\bp$ the set $\dP(\fR_\bp)=\setsuch{P_\bp\in\dP}{\fR_\bp(P_\bp)=\fR_\bp}$ is finite.

- For each vector rank $\fR_\bp$ all indecomposable complexes $(P_\bp,d_\bp)$ of projective $\bA$-modules of this vector rank, except finitely many isomorphism classes, are isomorphic to $P_\bp(m,\la)$ for some $P_\bp\in\dP$ and some $m,\la$.

The set $\dP$ is called a parameterizing set of $\bA$-complexes.

- We call an algebra $\bA$ derived wild if there is a bounded complex $(P_\bp,d_\bp)$ of projective modules over $\bA\*\Si$, where $\Si$ is the free $\Mk$-algebra in 2 variables, such that $\im d_n\subseteq\sJ P_{n-1}$ and, for any finite dimensional $\Si$-modules $L,L'$,

- $P_\bp\*_\Si L\iso P_\bp\*_\Si L'$ \iff $L\iso L'$.

- $P_\bp\*_\Si L$ is indecomposable \iff so is $L$.
card.label: Definition 1

paper.title: Derived tame local and two-point algebras
paper.abstract: We determine derived representation type of complete finitely generated local and two-point algebras over an algebraically closed field.
